subject: Real-time SLO pathing: Hosted vs Dedicated for QuickCart — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@quickcart.com>, Rohit Singh <rohit.singh@quickcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 15:05:00 -0500
Subject: Real-time SLO pathing: Hosted vs Dedicated for QuickCart — next steps

Hi Aisha / Rohit — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can pick the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated):

Key customer signals you shared:
- Target P95 inference latency: <= 50 ms for text classification + lightweight enrichment (avg request ~180 tokens).
- Steady-state QPS: ~200–250 sustained (peak bursts to ~500 during flash sales).
- Tight tail latency matters more than cost for the Checkout/Recommendation path.
- Legal/contract: procurement expects a 6–8 week procurement window; they asked about data separation options.

Initial assessment (from our side) — what aligns to Dedicated vs Hosted:
- Dedicated: gives predictable P95 under sustained QPS, configurable GPU pool, and private routing. Good fit if you want guaranteed tail SLOs and consistent latency for checkout.
- Hosted: cheaper for bursty workloads and faster to launch; works if warm cache and batching keep p95 in range and you accept occasional higher tail during cold starts or cross-tenant saturation.

Open technical questions for the team before we recommend a single path:
1) Typical request token distribution (we have the sample histogram but need P50/P95 token counts).
2) Expected concurrency per client (esp mobile vs web flows).
3) Can you tolerate short 200–300ms tail events during global peak if we implement Hosted + Dedicated fallback?
4) Any corporate requirement for dedicated tenancy/VPC or is contractual data separation via encryption/audit logs sufficient?

Proposed next steps (small pilot plan):
- QuickCart provides 3 days of representative traffic (headers scrubbed) OR run our synthetic runner against a staging endpoint we provision.
- Redwood deploys a Dedicated pilot config (3x A100-equivalent) and a Hosted pilot for comparison; we capture p50/p95/p99 across 24–72 hours.
- Deliverables: latency matrix (attached), MAP traces for problematic requests, and a recommendation memo.

Attachments: latency matrix (quickcart_latency_matrix.csv) and request traces (quickcart_trace_MAP.png).

If this sounds right, can Rohit confirm the dataset availability and Aisha confirm procurement timeline so we can lock pilot dates?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@quickcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rohit Singh <rohit.singh@quickcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Real-time SLO pathing: Hosted vs Dedicated for QuickCart — next steps

Ben — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers inline:
- Token distribution: P50 140 tokens, P95 320 tokens, P99 610 tokens (we pulled sampling from last 30 days).
- Concurrency: typical per-session concurrency is low, but our recommendation calls are highly bursty; per-IP concurrency can hit 6–8 during launches.
- Tail tolerance: for Checkout path we cannot exceed 100 ms P95 during normal ops; up to 200 ms may be tolerated for non-checkout recommendations.
- Data tenancy: Procurement prefers dedicated tenancy or strong contractual language + logging; they asked specifically for private VPC options.

We can schedule the pilot window — Rohit will share the scrubbed sample and procurement timeline. Procurement is targeting a signed SOW in ~7 weeks.

-Aisha
Aisha Malik | Head of ML Infrastructure | QuickCart
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Real-time SLO pathing: Hosted vs Dedicated for QuickCart — next steps

Perfect — thanks for the numbers, Aisha. Those P95/P99 token volumes explain the concern. Quick plan update based on your answers:

1) Pilot config: we will stand up a Dedicated pilot (reserve 3 x H100-equivalent with reserved KV-cache pool) tuned for low-latency, and also run an identical workload against our Hosted tier to capture cost/latency trade-offs. We expect Dedicated to be the baseline for Checkout path given the <=100 ms P95 requirement.

2) Load profile for the pilot: 250 sustained QPS (256-token avg) for 24 hours + burst simulation to 500 QPS for two 15-minute windows. Please confirm if this matches your expected pattern.

3) Metrics we will capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, per-request token counts, and end-to-end trace (MAP). We'll attach a decision checklist (QuickCart-decision-checklist.docx) summarizing pass/fail criteria.

4) Data tenancy: given procurement preference for dedicated tenancy/VPC, we will include the Private (VPC) path in the recommendation memo as option B if Dedicated cannot meet their contractual requirements. Private deployment has longer lead times; we will surface expected procurement and infra timelines.

Next asks (actionable):
- Rohit: drop scrubbed traffic sample into the Drive folder and confirm the dataplane egress policy for our staging endpoint (link above).
- Marissa: can you and Karthik own the Dedicated pilot setup? Plan for a preliminary run next week (Mon/Tue slot) so we can ship results to procurement.

Ben

---
Attachments referenced: quickcart_latency_matrix.csv, quickcart_trace_MAP.png, QuickCart-decision-checklist.docx
